raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What this does

Adds an opt-in `draft_context_window` to `--speculative-config` for DFlash and DSpark (MRV2). When set, the drafter only attends to the last N context tokens. Positions stay absolute. Target verification doesn't change. Default is `None`, so nothing changes unless you turn it on.

Context: #47930. We run Kimi K3 with `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on long agent sessions, and acceptance falls off a cliff past ~128K. This fixes it for us.

## Why

Accept length (k=3, out of 4) on main, DCP 1:

| context | main | main + `draft_context_window: 32768` |
|---|---|---|
| 0-16K | 2.48 | 2.49 |
| 16-64K | 2.39 | 2.40 |
| 64-128K | 2.29 | 2.27 |
| 128-256K | **1.45** | **2.29** |
| 256K+ | **1.26** | **2.22** |
| mixed 16-300K, c16 | 1.90 | 2.28 |

Below 128K: no change. Above it: back to short-context levels. Output tok/s goes up +31% at 128-256K and +23% at 256K+, +9% on the mixed run.

Same thing with DCP 4 (with #59392 applied, since main still crashes there, see below):

| context | main | window 32K |
|---|---|---|
| 64-128K | 2.26 | 2.29 |
| 128-256K | 1.46 | 2.28 |
| 256K+ | 1.26 | 2.20 |
| mixed c16 | 1.92 | 2.27 |

## Is it the kernel? No

Same build, no window, only the drafter's attention backend swapped:

| context | FLASHINFER_MLA | TRITON_MLA |
|---|---|---|
| 128-256K | 1.448 | 1.437 |
| 256K+ | 1.257 | 1.253 |

Same collapse on both. And on v0.30 it's the same with prefix caching and KV offload fully off (numbers in #47930), so it's not restored KV either. Looks like the drafter just doesn't generalise past what it was trained on (the model card only goes to ~95K). 64K behaves like 32K. I can't prove which shared bit is to blame (drafter weights vs. its RoPE/YaRN handling), but the window fixes it either way.

## Quality

GSM8K, first 200, `reasoning_effort: low`, temp 1.0:

| | main | window 32K |
|---|---|---|
| plain prompts (window never kicks in) | 0.985 | 0.990 |
| same problems behind a ~98K prefix (window drops ~65K) | 0.985 | 0.980 |

1 problem out of 200 either way. Noise.

## Soak

c24, prompts 16-400K, 30 min, same seed. Prefill-bound on purpose (pool oversubscribed).

| | main | window run A | window run B |
|---|---|---|---|
| requests | 331 | 341 | 345 |
| errors / restarts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| accept length | 1.61 | 2.27 | 2.27 |
| output tok/s | 130 | 153 | 146 |
| TTFT p50 | 58 s | 48 s | 47 s |

No shm_broadcast hangs after load, no Xid. One heads-up: our repeated-tail detector flagged one output in run A (129K prompt, ran to `max_tokens`). Didn't capture the text that time, so I couldn't look at it. Run B captured text and flagged nothing. 1 in 686 vs 0 in 331, so no conclusion either way. The shift can't reach target inputs or target KV (more below), and with probabilistic drafting the output distribution doesn't depend on the drafter anyway.

## How it works

In `DFlashSpeculator.propose`, right after `prepare_dflash_inputs` has computed slot mappings from the full table, a small Triton kernel does, per request:

- excess = `max(seq_len - num_query - N, 0)`, rounded down to whole block-table entries
- shift that request's `input_block_tables[gid]` row left by that many entries
- subtract the dropped positions from `seq_lens`

Keys already carry absolute RoPE, query positions aren't touched, so relative positions inside the window are unchanged. Draft sees at least N tokens, less than N plus one entry.

Why editing those buffers in place is fine:
- `input_block_tables` get re-gathered from the persistent tables at the start of every step, before the target runs. Nothing after `propose` reads them in the same step.
- `seq_lens` is the draft's own buffer.
- Slot mappings are computed before the shift, so KV writes land where they should.
- Dummy runs (capture, profiling) skip it.

DCP: one entry covers `block_size * dcp_size` positions, and `block_size % cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 0` is already enforced, so whole entries keep every position on its rank. Draft KV groups share `seq_lens`, so all groups drop the same count (a multiple of `dcp_size * lcm(block sizes)`), and only the last one writes it back.

CUDA graphs: runs eagerly before replay and only writes buffers the graph already reads. No new host syncs.

Scope: all DFlash-family speculators go through this `propose`, so it covers `dflash` and `dspark`. Rejected for other methods and on V1, so it never gets silently ignored. Only measured on DSpark / Kimi K3 (MLA drafter). Non-MLA drafters take the same path with `dcp_size=1`, which the unit tests cover.

Tradeoffs: you lose long-range context the drafter could in theory use. For this drafter that's a net loss past ~128K anyway. The right N depends on the drafter, hence off by default. No memory saved, only attention is bounded.

## Related

- #47930: the issue. Our data there shows the collapse with nothing restored.
- #47926: hides prefix-cache-restored blocks from the draft. On this model those blocks hold valid draft KV, so it only helps by accident (shorter context). Hand-rebased on 0.30 it got 2.07 / 1.89 vs 2.30 / 2.25 for the window. Independent of this PR.
- #53827: similar bounded draft attention for EAGLE3 via sliding window. Different speculator and path. Happy to align the field name if both land.
- #60320: trims DSpark context precompute for all-SWA drafters. Compute-only, complementary.
- Side note: main still can't boot Kimi K3 + DSpark with DCP>1 on FlashInfer MLA (#59065). Our DCP 4 runs used #59392.

## Tests

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD                 # all pass
pytest tests/test_config.py -k draft_context_window -v               # CPU: 1 passed
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -v         # B300: 10 passed (5 old + 5 new)
```

`tests/test_config.py -k "spec or draft or dflash or dspark"`: 97 passed, 5 failed. The same 5 fail on untouched main on this CPU box (three `test_vllm_config_defaults[RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3-*]`, `test_draft_model_enables_async_scheduling_by_default`, `test_dflash_allows_async_scheduling`).

Rebased onto main 642c18d64 on 2026-10-16. The one conflict was in `vllm/config/vllm.py`, where #59973 added a line to the same V1 unsupported list; both are kept. #59511 moved the context combine and `prepare_context_anchor` into the FULL graph. Neither reads the draft `seq_lens` or block tables the window shifts, and the context K/V slots are still computed from the full table before the shift. After the rebase, pre-commit passes, and `test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` gives 10 passed on CPU under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`; with the window turned into a no-op, the 5 new tests fail.

New tests: window applied after slot mappings (through `propose`, DCP 1 and 2), whole-entry rounding, two groups with different block sizes, a long in-place shift across kernel chunks, and config validation.

GPU setup: TP8 on 8x B300, Kimi K3 fp8 KV, k=3, probabilistic drafting + block rejection. `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-fe4df3df0` with the spec-decode files overlaid from this branch's base, so the draft path equals main. Synthetic multi-turn agent sessions over public-domain text, natural stop, `max_tokens` 2048, prefix caching and KV offload on.

+| `draft_context_window` | `integer >= 1` | `None` | Limit the draft's attention to at least the most recent N context tokens, dropping older ones in whole KV cache blocks (times the DCP size). @@ -218,3 +225,112 @@ def test_prepare_dflash_inputs_never_writes_the_null_block():
         PAD_SLOT_ID,
         PAD_SLOT_ID,
     ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "cp_rank,cp_size,block_table_values,shifted_entries",
+    [(0, 1, [0, 0, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12], [7, 8]), (1, 2, [0, 7, 8, 9], [7])],

+def test_draft_context_window_applies_after_slot_mappings(
+    cp_rank, cp_size, block_table_values, shifted_entries
+):
+    # Context ends at position 11, so the draft length is 15. A window of 4
+    # drops 8 positions: two entries of 4, or one entry of 4 x DCP 2.
+    kwargs = dict(
+        target_positions=[10, 11, 12, 13],
+        block_table_values=block_table_values,
+        cp_rank=cp_rank,
+        cp_size=cp_size,
+        cp_interleave=2,
+    )
+    full = _run_prepare(**kwargs)
+    windowed = _run_prepare(**kwargs, draft_context_window=4)
+
+    assert full.input_buffers.seq_lens[0].item() == 15
+    assert windowed.input_buffers.seq_lens[0].item() == 7
+    num_shifted = len(shifted_entries)
+    assert windowed.block_table[0][:num_shifted].tolist() == shifted_entries
+    assert windowed.query_slot_mapping.tolist() == full.query_slot_mapping.tolist()
+    assert windowed.context_slot_mapping.tolist() == full.context_slot_mapping.tolist()
+
+
+def _drop_old_context(
+    seq_lens: list[int],
+    block_table: list[list[int]],
+    *,
+    context_window: int,
+    window_span: int,
+    entry_span: int,
+    update_seq_lens: bool = True,
+    num_query_per_req: int = 4,
+):
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    seq_lens_t = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    block_table_t = torch.tensor(block_table, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    drop_old_draft_context(
+        block_table_t,
+        seq_lens_t,
+        len(seq_lens),
+        num_query_per_req,
+        context_window,
+        window_span,
+        entry_span,
+        update_seq_lens=update_seq_lens,
+    )
+    return seq_lens_t.tolist(), block_table_t.tolist()
+
+
+def test_draft_context_window_drops_whole_entries():
+    # block_size 4 x DCP 2: one entry covers 8 positions. Request 0 has 83
+    # context tokens, so 64 are dropped and 19 (>= the window of 16) stay
+    # visible. Request 1 fits in the window and the padded row is untouched.
+    rows = [list(range(100, 116)), list(range(200, 216)), list(range(300, 316))]
+    seq_lens, block_table = _drop_old_context(
+        [87, 20, 0], rows, context_window=16, window_span=8, entry_span=8
+    )
+
+    assert seq_lens == [23, 20, 0]
+    assert block_table[0][:3] == [108, 109, 110]
+    assert block_table[1:] == rows[1:]
+
+
+def test_draft_context_window_shifts_groups_with_different_block_sizes():
+    # Groups with block sizes 4 and 8 drop the same 24 positions (a multiple
+    # of their lcm), and only the last group rewrites the shared seq_lens.
+    seq_lens = [40]
+    small, large = [list(range(100, 116))], [list(range(200, 208))]
+
+    seq_lens, small = _drop_old_context(
+        seq_lens,
+        small,
+        context_window=10,
+        window_span=8,
+        entry_span=4,
+        update_seq_lens=False,
+    )
+    assert seq_lens == [40]
+    seq_lens, large = _drop_old_context(
+        seq_lens, large, context_window=10, window_span=8, entry_span=8
+    )
+

         CP_INTERLEAVE=cp_interleave,
         BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE,
     )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _drop_old_draft_context_kernel(
+    block_table_ptr,
+    block_table_stride,
+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    num_query_per_req,
+    context_window,
+    window_span,
+    entry_span,
+    UPDATE_SEQ_LENS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    req_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + req_idx)
+    num_excess = tl.maximum(seq_len - num_query_per_req - context_window, 0)
+    num_dropped = num_excess // window_span * window_span
+    if num_dropped == 0:
+        return
+    shift = num_dropped // entry_span
+    num_kept = tl.minimum(
+        tl.cdiv(seq_len - num_dropped, entry_span), block_table_stride - shift
+    )
+    row_ptr = block_table_ptr + req_idx.to(tl.int64) * block_table_stride
+    for i in range(0, num_kept, BLOCK_SIZE):
+        offset = i + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+        mask = offset < num_kept
+        block_ids = tl.load(row_ptr + shift + offset, mask=mask)
+        # In-place shift: every lane must load before any lane stores.
+        tl.debug_barrier()
+        tl.store(row_ptr + offset, block_ids, mask=mask)
+    if UPDATE_SEQ_LENS:
+        tl.store(seq_lens_ptr + req_idx, seq_len - num_dropped)
+
+
+def drop_old_draft_context(
+    # [max_num_reqs, max_num_blocks]
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    # [max_num_reqs]
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    num_reqs: int,
+    num_query_per_req: int,
+    context_window: int,
+    window_span: int,
+    entry_span: int,
+    update_seq_lens: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Hide all but the last ``context_window`` context tokens from the draft.
+
+    Drops the oldest context positions in multiples of ``window_span`` by
+    shifting each request's block-table row left, so the draft attends to at
+    least ``context_window`` and fewer than ``context_window + window_span``
+    context tokens. ``entry_span`` is the number of positions one entry of this
+    table covers (block_size * dcp_size). Cached keys hold absolute RoPE
+    positions, so no position needs rewriting. ``seq_lens`` must hold the
+    unshifted draft lengths; it is rewritten only when ``update_seq_lens`` is
+    set, which callers do on the last of several tables sharing it.
+    """
+    _drop_old_draft_context_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+        block_table,
+        block_table.stride(0),
+        seq_lens,
+        num_query_per_req,
+        context_window,
+        window_span,
+        entry_span,
+        UPDATE_SEQ_LENS=update_seq_lens,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=1024,
+    )
